issues: Ancient astrology claims of birth complications, obstetric danger and maternal death are historically unvalidated and must never inform clinical or pregnancy decisions.
The original oblique/long ascension sign glyphs and right-ascension family classifications require specialist verification before computerized chart rules.
Dangerous childbirth is a compound oblique Ascendant plus affliction or node condition; it is not simply a sign-based birth risk.
Favorable delivery is offered through several partially overlapping alternatives, allowing extensive retrospective choice of apparent successes.
The manuscript uses different zodiac signs for men's and women's natal charts, period sex/gender categories and no actual birth records.
Mars/Saturn condition in twelfth, slow/retrograde/stationary and Moon-in-oblique condition, tenth ruler in eighth are different source branches.
No human pregnancy care records, duration of labor, birth outcome, mother-child survival, era-correct maternal death baseline or controls were supplied.
The author 'may be doubted' maternal childbirth mortality claim is hedged, not a quantified prospective risk or direct prediction.
No clinical use, pregnancy monitoring or medication/surgical interpretation is permitted from such source hypotheses.
The subsequent printed CXXIIII on paternal inheritance begins later on the SAME frame606 and has separate substantive original source rules.
Original source images and selective brief anchors are preserved; no full diplomatic glyph transcription or human-prospectively tested accuracy.
